title: network-evidence-mini-ux-and-rollback-lane-prd
body:
Purpose and context:
This is an early PRD sketch for a compact network evidence handoff UX and a lightweight rollback lane aimed at customer-managed networking within Private deployments. The goal is to reduce on-call friction during network changes while providing minimal, verifiable audit artifacts that satisfy common SOC/infra audits without forcing full heavy-weight evidence bundles for every small change.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Customers running Redwood Private often push small firewall/peering changes that require operator sign-off and produce large audit payloads (costly to store and slow to review).
- On-call and operator teams want a quick way to confirm changes and trigger a safe rollback if telemetry shows regressions.
- Security/compliance teams want cryptographic continuity (proof-of-change) and a compact searchable index for postmortems.
- Current designs create a binary choice: full attestation (heavy) or no evidence (risky). We need a middle path.

Primary goals (MUST):
- Define a compact evidence artifact (mini-evidence) that captures the minimal fields needed for verification and forensic replay.
- Provide operator UX flows for "approve-with-quick-evidence" and "approve-with-rollback-lane" integrated into the onboarding console and CLI.
- Implement sample-based audit retention that keeps full evidence for a fraction of changes and compact artifacts for all.
- Ensure artifacts are signed with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or with delegated attestation tokens, depending on deployment mode.

Secondary goals (SHOULD):
- Developer-friendly API to fetch summarized evidence and reconstruct a timeline for a change window.
- First-pass analytics on rollback triggers: detect patterns and provide recommended safety thresholds.
- Low-bandwidth option for on-prem customers where evidence upload may be deferred but anchored.

User personas:
- Customer Network Operator (CNO): makes and reviews changes. Needs fast sign-off and an easy rollback trigger.
- Customer Security Auditor (CSA): needs verifiable chain-of-proof, searchable compact index for investigations.
- Redwood SRE/Support: occasionally investigates incidents across customers; needs a consistent minimal artifact shape to triage faster.

Key user stories:
- As a CNO, I can approve a VPC-peering change with a single signed mini-evidence artifact and a checkbox to create a rollback-lane for 30 minutes.
- As a CNO, I can trigger an automated rollback from the console within the defined rollback window; the action emits a rollback evidence artifact.
- As a CSA, I can query a compact index (time range + change id) and retrieve a signed summary plus pointers to full evidence if retained.
- As Redwood SRE, I can optionally request a full evidence pull for a given change id when investigating anomalies; the request is gated and audited.

Functional requirements (high level):
1) Mini-evidence artifact schema (compact):
   - change_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), actor (email/orig-system), diff_summary (text, <= 512 chars), risk_score (float 0-1), rollback_token (opaque), signature (base64), evidence_retention_level (enum: full|mini|none), verification_anchor (sha256 digest or KMS reference).
   - The schema must be serializable as a newline-delimited JSON for easy streaming.

2) Rollback lane primitives:
   - When a change is approved with rollback enabled, a rollback_token is issued that can be used to invoke an idempotent rollback API endpoint.
   - Rollback tokens expire (configurable, default 30m). Triggering rollback generates a rollback-evidence artifact.
   - Rollback endpoints are rate-limited and require both token + operator confirmation for high-risk changes.

3) Sampling and retention policy:
   - By default keep mini artifacts for all changes for 365 days.
   - Sample 1 in N (configurable, default N=20) changes for full evidence retention (payloads, snapshots).
   - Allow customer to opt into higher sampling or pin specific change_ids for permanent archival.

4) Signing and anchoring:
   - Support two modes: customer-KMS signing (preferred for Private) and Redwood-signed attestations for hosted-assist operations.
   - All signatures must include a key-id and public key reference stored in the tenant metadata.

5) UX/Console flows:
   - Approve change modal with: "quick-evidence" summary, toggle: enable rollback (30m/1h/4h), optional free-text justification, and checkbox 'anchor now' to request immediate full evidence capture (may cost extra).
   - Timeline view for each change showing mini-evidence, sampled full evidence markers, and rollback actions.

Non-functional requirements:
- Compact artifacts should be <4KB on average.
- Verification path (fetch signature, verify with keyref) should complete in <500ms for UI flows.
- Storage overhead must be <5% of current logging pipeline costs assuming default sampling.
- Backfill/repair: a mechanism to re-anchor evidence after network failures (deferred upload queue).

Success metrics (proposed):
- Mean time to verify a change (CNO) falls below 2 minutes for 90% of approvals.
- Fraction of on-call rollbacks successfully executed within window >= 95% for first 30 days.
- Customer satisfaction (NPS/CSAT) on onboarding network changes increases by 15 points for pilot customers.
- Audit request fulfillment time for compact index < 1 hour for 95% of requests.

Implementation sketch (phases):
Phase 0 (spike, 2 wks):
- Prototype mini-evidence JSON schema and signature flow using local KMS emulator.
- Build minimal console modal mock and CLI knob to test operator flows with a subset of customers.

Phase 1 (MVP, 6 wks):
- Implement artifact generation, signature plumbing for customer-KMS and Redwood-sign mode.
- Basic rollback lane: token issuance, rollback endpoint, and evidence emission.
- Sampling engine basic config and retention defaults.
- Console UX basic modal + timeline placeholder.

Phase 2 (hardening, 8 wks):
- Integrate deferred upload queue, storage cost telemetry, and compact index for quick queries.
- Add HSM/KMS rotation support and key reference UI.
- Implement audit request workflow with RBAC and escalation logging.

Open questions and trade-offs (to resolve):
- Do we allow rollback tokens to be exported to customer automation (webhooks/terraform)? Risks: token leakage. Possible mitigation: scoped tokens, IP allowlist, short TTL.
- Sampling rate economics: how to balance storage cost vs. investigator time? Need pricing/commit model.
- For on-prem air-gapped installs, can we allow offline anchoring with later reconciliation? Design needed for proof-of-origin if time-separated.
- How much free-text justification do auditors actually need vs structured fields? Extra fields increase artifact size.

Safety and compliance notes:
- All consented data fields must honor tenant data retention policy.
- Signatures and keys are part of customer security review; include KMS attestability documentation in the final PRD.

Next steps (immediate):
- Schedule 1hr sync with infra and SRE to validate rollback endpoint constraints (Marcus/Chen/Ellen).
- Create spike tickets: PDP-4123 (mini-evidence spike), PDP-4124 (rollback token proto).
- Identify two pilot customers (one cloud VPC, one on-prem) and prepare test plan.

Notes to self / TODOs (rough):
- Draft minimal audit index API (search by actor/change_id/range) and include cost model.
- Align with legal on signature acceptability for audits in EU/UK jurisdictions.
- Add sample mini-evidence payloads to the Confluence prototyping page.

Recent references and links:
- see linked artifacts above for the working spike threads.
- sketch: github.com/redwood-inference/prototypes/mini-evidence

End of draft.

(Free-form roughness intentionally included — looking for product + infra feedback on rollback semantics and sampling economics.)
